item.title: How to Prevent Prompt Injection Attacks: From Detection to Mitigation Prompt injection attacks exploit missing trust boundaries in LLMs to override instructions and cause real-world harm, and cannot be stopped with prompts alone. Effective defense requires layered controls for detection, mitigation, and protection enforced outside the model to limit damage and prevent escalation.
item.description:
Author: Fergal Glynn
Date: January 06, 2026
Tags: ["Cybersecurity", "Artificial Intelligence", "Large Language Models", "Prompt Injection Attacks", "Threat Detection and Mitigation"]
Summary:
  • Prompt injection attacks exploit trust gaps in large language models.
  • These attacks can bypass safeguards and cause harm.
  • Defense requires detection, mitigation, and protection layers.
  • Detection finds suspicious inputs or outputs early.
  • Mitigation limits damage after an attack occurs.
  • Protection enforces strict boundaries outside the model.
